growth_signal.value: Backed by Visa and Circle, and named in coverage of Circle's Q4 earnings as one of the stablecoin partners it invested in.

entry.idea: Businesses that hold or get paid in stablecoins have no easy way to use that money for everyday treasury and settlement, so Velocity builds payment infrastructure that lets businesses tap into stablecoins for cross-border money movement.
entry.lesson: As stablecoins go mainstream, build the business-facing plumbing (treasury and settlement) instead of another consumer wallet or exchange.
entry.name: Velocity

growth.basis: substitute: raised a large funding round from strategic investors Visa and Circle
growth.reason: No user or revenue numbers are public, but it raised a sizeable $38 million round backed by Visa and Circle.

market.reason: Cross-border business payments and settlement is a huge worldwide market that touches nearly every company that trades internationally.

tech.reason: Building stablecoin settlement rails for businesses is solid engineering, but it competes with several other well-funded stablecoin infrastructure startups doing similar things.

sources.title: Exclusive: Payments startup Velocity raises $38 million to help businesses tap stablecoin growth

entry.twist: It positions itself as a direct competitor to banks and foreign-exchange firms for business settlement, not just another crypto tool for crypto-native companies.
entry.who_pays: Businesses that want faster, cheaper cross-border payments and treasury tools pay to use Velocity's platform.
entry.why_now: Stablecoin volumes are growing fast and businesses want cheaper, faster cross-border payments than banks and FX houses can offer.
